citation.title: Development of Fast Charge Exchange Recombination Spectroscopy by Using Interference Filter Method in JT-60U
citation.authors: Kobayashi, S.; Sakasai, A.; Koide, Y.; Sakamoto, Y.; Kamada, Y.; Hatae, T.; Oyama, N.; Miura, Y.

topic: Fast carbon-impurity (CVI 529.05 nm) CXRS on JT-60U using 3- and 7-channel interference-filter photomultiplier assemblies, compared with a CCD spectrometer
own_question: Can filter-based CXRS resolve fast impurity Ti and rotation changes during minor collapses and ELMs, and does the 3-filter Gaussian assumption hold?
actual_method_and_evidence: Intensity ratios I1/I2 and I3/I2 are mapped to Ti and Vr through precomputed polynomial fits that assume a Maxwellian line shape, with no nonlinear fitting. Integration was 0.8 ms for the 3-filter system, compared with 16.7 ms minimum (50 ms summed in the example) for CCD CXRS. Evidence comes from single reversed-shear minor-collapse and type-I ELM H-mode examples, with qualitative agreement against CCD. Seven-filter spectra appeared Gaussian on a few-ms scale. At S/N of about 4, the estimated errors were about 30% in Ti and 25 km/s in rotation. Real-time feedback through RTP was only planned.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Conventional CCD-based CES has limited time resolution; on JT-60U the minimum was 16.7 ms, which motivated hardware approaches to faster impurity-Ti measurement.
claim_checks.qualification: JT-60U-specific hardware; this concerns carbon impurity Ti, not main-ion Ti; it is a measurement upgrade, not nowcasting.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Upstream methods that avoid nonlinear spectral fitting, such as filter intensity-ratio mapping, have been proposed as candidates for real-time Ti estimation.
claim_checks.qualification: Feedback control was planned, not demonstrated. The method assumes Gaussian line shapes and has large errors at low S/N. Eq.(3) extracted imperfectly.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The source's inputs were filter photomultiplier intensities and its targets were CVI Ti and rotation, measured offline per frame. It contains no past-only prediction and gives no report arrival latency.
validation_if_relevant: Validation is qualitative comparison against CCD CXRS and 7-filter spectra in a few discharges. There are no held-out splits and no statistical skill metrics.
forbidden_inferences: The source did not achieve real-time control.
The source is not KSTAR evidence.
The source does not establish that the Gaussian assumption holds in general.
The source does not show that faster upstream CES removes the need for nowcasting.
The source does not provide physical-truth Ti.
The source does not address BES/ECEI information.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as background on the upstream route to faster impurity CES: faster hardware and fit-free reading. It contrasts with our downstream causal nowcast of the current report, and it shows the label-noise limits of fast CES.
